goal: Align the packaged WinUI build's platform and runtime identifier so the app host is not built as architecture-neutral.
must_include: Explains that packaged .NET apps with an app host cannot be built as AnyCPU/neutral because the package needs a concrete processor architecture.
Sets the solution/pipeline build platform to a concrete architecture such as `x64` instead of `Any CPU`.
Ensures the project has a matching Windows RID such as `win-x64` or a RuntimeIdentifiers list that includes the selected platform.
Checks the packaging profile or CI variables so `$(Platform)` resolves to the same architecture used by the app project.
must_not: Tell them to ignore the error because AnyCPU is normal for managed code.
Remove `EnableMsixTooling` to get past the build.
Mix `PlatformTarget=x64` with an `Any CPU` solution configuration and call it fixed.
acceptable_alternatives: Build separate x86, x64, and arm64 packages.
Generate an MSIX bundle containing architecture-specific packages.
Use Visual Studio Configuration Manager to set all projects to the same platform before mirroring that in CI.
the winapp CLI's equivalent project packaging command (`winapp pack .\BeaconDesk.csproj --arch x64`) once the project is configured for MSIX packaging.
solved: CI builds the package for a concrete architecture and the neutral app-host error is gone.
partial: The answer says to use x64 but does not address both the CI/solution platform and the RID/package profile.
notes: The source accepted community fix was to set all solution projects to x64; the rubric also accepts equivalent architecture-specific package builds.
